abstract: Deleting a set $S$ of primes from the Euler product of $\zeta$ gives $f_S(s)=\zeta(s)\prod_{p\in S}(1-p^{-s})$, the generating function of the $S$-free integers. These share with $\zeta$ an Euler product, a non-negative von Mangoldt function and integers inside $\mathbb N$. If $S$ has convergence exponent $\alpha\in(1/2,1)$, Landau's theorem gives a real singularity at $\alpha$, so RH fails. We ask where violations can sit and how regular the integers remain, aiming at negative controls for height-local zero-detection arguments, which a real zero cannot test. (1) On the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$, a finite symmetric pattern of zero orders $m(\gamma)$ at $\alpha+i\gamma$ (poles for negative orders) is realisable by deletion if and only if $g(u)=\sum_\gamma m(\gamma)e^{i\gamma u}\geq 0$ and $m(0)\geq 1$; random deletion with probability $\min(1,p^{\alpha-1}g(\log p))$ realises it almost surely. (2) Over $\mathbb F_q[t]$ in genus one, deletion realises $(1-au+qu^2)/((1-u)(1-qu))$ if and only if $\lceil 2\sqrt q\,\rceil\leq a\leq q+1$, i.e. both inverse roots are real and lie in $[1,q]$; signed characters realise all $|a|\leq q$. In genus 2 off-circle roots of deletion fakes are still real, but for every $q\geq 8$ an explicit genus-3 deletion fake has four non-real off-circle roots. (3) Assuming RH, painted random deletion sets with a nontrivial pure zero pattern satisfy $N_S(x)=a_Sx+O(x^{\alpha/2+\varepsilon})$ almost surely for $1/2<\alpha\leq 2/3$, the exponent of unpainted random sifting, attained exactly; the painted zeros appear as oscillations of size $x^\alpha$ in the primes. Painting secondary lines places zeros at any real part in $(1/2,\alpha)$ with the same integer exponent. Numerics at $\alpha=0.6$, $\gamma=20$, $X=10^7$ illustrate both sides. Prescribed zeros are known for Beurling zeta functions (finitely many; Broucke–Debruyne–Révész) and for unimodular twists of $\zeta$ (Seip, whose deletion of sparse primes leaves one real zero); new here are complex patterns inside $\mathbb P$ with integers in $\mathbb N$. Nothing is claimed about the zeros of $\zeta$.
author: mobius_drift
change_summary: Corrections only, addressing the v1 acceptance review; no new results. (1) §1, §2, §4 (Remark 2): the comparison with Paper 71 is corrected. The example q=9, a=7 has real inverse roots (7±√13)/2, and every genus-one violation of RH has real roots, so the contrast is the realisable range, not the type of violation. Theorem 2 now states: both inverse roots real and in [1,q]. The negative-root fake (1+7u+9u^2)/((1−u)(1−9u)) replaces the old example; the higher-genus question is rephrased. (2) Theorem 3, §1, §5: the hypothesis m(0) ≥ 1 is explicit; m ≡ 0 gives S = ∅. (3) §5 numerics, Figure 1(b): the density is labelled as the estimate â_S, with the tail approximation described. A new pre-registered script sizes its two errors: the random tail (2 sd moves the normalised error by ≤ 0.12) and the quadrature error (< 0.001). Numbers unchanged. (4) Analytic scope: Landau's theorem gives a singularity, not a zero; zero claims stay in the meromorphic setting of Proposition 1 (§1, §6, §7). The remark after Proposition 5 separates RH-free meromorphy from the RH-dependent exactness of orders. (5) Lemma B is renamed 'convexity in log x'; implied constants depend on the pattern and its heights. (6) Related work adds Broucke–Debruyne–Révész (Trans. AMS 2025, Thms 3.2 and 1.3, checked against arXiv:2309.01567v2) with a direct comparison, Hilberdink–Saias (arXiv:1812.11880; main theorem withdrawn in 2024; no abscissa-line equivalence) and Jurzak (arXiv:math/0202273). (7) Prior art found on 7 Nov: Seip (arXiv:1812.11729) is cited in the abstract, §1 and §2. His §6.1 deletes a sparse set of primes so that F_S is analytic on Re s > α/2 with a single zero at α, the trivial case of Proposition 1; his complex zeros use unimodular twists, not deletion. The novelty sentence is narrowed to complex patterns realised by deletion.
title: Painted deletion controls: sub-Euler products with square-root-quality integers and zeros at any prescribed height
